content: The term RUQ refers to the right-upper quadrant of the human abdomen. This anatomical region is used by medical professionals to localize and assess pain, tenderness, scars, lumps, or other abnormalities of clinical interest. The RUQ is anatomically defined as the area extending from the median plane to the right side of the patient and from the umbilical plane to the right ribcage. Pain or tenderness in the RUQ can be indicative of various medical conditions, including hepatitis, cholecystitis, and peptic ulcer disease. These conditions often involve organs located within this quadrant, such as the liver, gallbladder, and portions of the stomach and intestines. The term RUQ is specific to human anatomy and is not typically used in comparative anatomy, as most other animals do not maintain an upright posture. In veterinary medicine, the equivalent term for this region in quadrupedal animals is right anterior quadrant.
